records.source: לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲבָנִ֥ים אֵין֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־יוֹרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ מַדּ֗וּעַ יָרַ֤שׁ מַלְכָּם֙ אֶת־גָּ֔ד וְעַמּ֖וֹ בְּעָרָ֥יו יָשָֽׁב׃
records.gloss: Concerning [the] sons of Ammon. Thus says the LORD: Sons [are there] not to Israel? Or an heir [is there] not to him? Why has their king taken possession of Gad, and his people in its cities has settled?
pieces: Concerning the Ammonites. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Has Israel no {{gender:children|sons}}? \q Has it no heir? \q Then why has Milcom taken over Gad, \q and why do his people live in its towns?

L.1: Concerning the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon. Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Has Israel no {{gender:children|sons}}? \q Has he no heir? \q Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad, \q and his people settled in its cities?

R.1: About the Ammonites. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Does Israel have no children? \q Is there no one to inherit its land? \q Then why has Milcom, the god of the Ammonites, taken over the land of Gad? \q Why do his people live in Gad's towns?

decisions.choice: Concerning the sons of Ammon: the heading of an oracle about the Ammonites
decisions.reason: The oracles against the nations (chapters 46-51) are headed by the name of each people. The Ammonites lived east of the Jordan, around their capital Rabbah (verse 2). They were descended from Lot (Genesis 19:38) and were often at war with Israel (Judges 11; 2 Samuel 10). The oracle on Ammon runs from verse 1 to verse 6.

decisions.choice: Milcom, the national god of the Ammonites
alternatives: their king (the king of the Ammonites)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can be read "their king", as the vowels of the traditional text have it, or as Milcom, the name of the Ammonite god (1 Kings 11:5, 33; 2 Kings 23:13). The word returns in verse 3, where it goes into exile "with his priests and his officials"; that fits a god best, and 48:7 says the same of Chemosh, the god of Moab. The Greek translation reads a name here and in verse 3 (stated from general knowledge). Either way, Ammon's god and the king who served him stand behind the seizing of Israel's land.

decisions.choice: Gad: the Israelite tribe east of the Jordan, whose land Ammon had taken
decisions.reason: Gad held land east of the Jordan, next to Ammon (Numbers 32:33-36; Joshua 13:24-28). When Assyria took the people of that region into exile (2 Kings 15:29), Ammon moved in. The questions play on the word "heir" and the verb "take possession", which come from one root: Israel still has heirs, so Ammon had no right to inherit Gad's land.

decisions.choice: Milcom ... the god of the Ammonites
alternatives: their king
decisions.reason: Every level gives the name; Readable adds who Milcom is, since most readers will not know (m2).

decisions.choice: children / sons
decisions.reason: The question means descendants who can inherit; the gender setting gives "sons" as the traditional form. The heading's "sons of Ammon" is the Ammonite people, as in 25:21.

records.heading: Ammon

records.source: לָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּה֩ יָמִ֨ים בָּאִ֜ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה וְ֠הִשְׁמַעְתִּי אֶל־רַבַּ֨ת בְּנֵי־עַמּ֜וֹן תְּרוּעַ֣ת מִלְחָמָ֗ה וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְתֵ֣ל שְׁמָמָ֔ה וּבְנֹתֶ֖יהָ בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּצַּ֑תְנָה וְיָרַ֧שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־יֹרְשָׁ֖יו אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore look days [are] coming, declares the LORD, and I will cause to be heard against Rabbah of [the] sons of Ammon a shout of battle, and it will become a mound of desolation, and its daughters with fire will be burned; and will dispossess Israel its dispossessors, says the LORD.
pieces: So the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make the battle cry ring out against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a mound of ruins, \q and its villages will go up in flames. \q Then Israel will drive out those who drove it out, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make a battle shout heard against Rabbah of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, and it will become a desolate mound; \q and its daughters will be burned with fire, \q and Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: So the time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make the people of Rabbah, the Ammonite capital, hear the shouts of battle. Rabbah will become a heap of ruins, \q and the villages around it will burn. \q Then Israel will take back its land from those who took it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Rabbah: the capital city of the Ammonites, left a ruin mound
decisions.reason: Rabbah stood where the city of Amman, in Jordan, is today (Deuteronomy 3:11; 2 Samuel 12:26-31). A "mound" (tel) is the heap left when a city is destroyed and not rebuilt, as in Joshua 8:28.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller towns and villages that belonged to the city
decisions.reason: Hebrew calls the villages around a city its "daughters" (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45).

decisions.choice: Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed it: Israel will take back its land from those who took it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 1 for Milcom "taking possession" of Gad. Those who seized Israel's land will lose it to Israel. Jeremiah's word for the conquest of Canaan is the same (Deuteronomy 9:1).

decisions.choice: drive out those who drove it out / take back its land from those who took it
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the repeated verb with a common English verb; Readable says what the repetition means (m3). Literal keeps "dispossess".

decisions.choice: the Ammonite capital
decisions.reason: Readable says what Rabbah was (m1).

records.source: הֵילִ֨ילִי חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן כִּ֣י שֻׁדְּדָה־עַ֗י צְעַקְנָה֮ בְּנ֣וֹת רַבָּה֒ חֲגֹ֣רְנָה שַׂקִּ֔ים סְפֹ֕דְנָה וְהִתְשׁוֹטַ֖טְנָה בַּגְּדֵר֑וֹת כִּ֤י מַלְכָּם֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֣ה יֵלֵ֔ךְ כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו יַחְדָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: Wail, Heshbon, for is devastated Ai; cry out, daughters of Rabbah, gird yourselves [with] sackcloth, lament, and run to and fro among the walls; for their king into exile will go, his priests and his princes together.
pieces: Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry out, you villages of Rabbah! \q Put on sackcloth \q and mourn; \q run back and forth inside the stone walls! \q For Milcom will go into exile, \q and his priests and officials with him.

L.3: Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated; cry out, daughters of Rabbah! \q Put on sackcloth; \q lament, \q and run to and fro among the walls! \q For Milcom will go into exile, \q his priests and his princes together.

R.3: Cry out in grief, Heshbon, for Ai is destroyed! Scream, you villages around Rabbah! \q Put on sackcloth \q and mourn. \q Run here and there inside the stone fences. \q For Milcom, your god, will be carried off to a foreign land, \q and his priests and leaders with him.

decisions.choice: Heshbon and Ai: towns of Ammon in this oracle
alternatives: Ai: read as a common noun, "the ruin"
decisions.reason: Heshbon had once been the city of Sihon king of the Amorites (Numbers 21:26) and is named among Moab's towns in 48:2, 34; at this time it seems to have been in Ammonite hands. This Ai is not the Ai near Bethel (Joshua 7-8) but a place in Ammon not otherwise known. Its name means "heap of ruins", which suits the line.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and lament: the signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Rough goat-hair cloth was worn next to the skin in grief (4:8; 6:26). The commands are feminine plural: the "daughters", Rabbah's villages (verse 2), are called to mourn like women at a funeral.

decisions.choice: run to and fro among the walls: rush about inside the stone walls of the sheepfolds, with nowhere to hide
alternatives: run about with gashes (cuts made in mourning), reading a word that differs by one letter
decisions.reason: The word means walls of loose stone, such as sheepfolds or field walls (Numbers 32:16). People fleeing the city run back and forth among them. A similar word means cuts made on the body in mourning (48:37), and some suggest that reading, but the text as it stands makes sense.

decisions.choice: Milcom will go into exile: the god of Ammon is carried off with his priests
decisions.reason: Conquerors carried away the images of the gods of defeated peoples. A god led away captive is shown to be powerless; 48:7 says the same of Chemosh, and Isaiah 46:1-2 of the gods of Babylon. On the name, see verse 1.

decisions.choice: Cry out in grief
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Readable says "Cry out in grief" for "Wail".

decisions.choice: villages of Rabbah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "daughters" are, as in verse 2. Literal keeps "daughters".

records.source: מַה־תִּתְהַֽלְלִי֙ בָּֽעֲמָקִ֔ים זָ֣ב עִמְקֵ֔ךְ הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה הַבֹּֽטְחָה֙ בְּאֹ֣צְרֹתֶ֔יהָ מִ֖י יָב֥וֹא אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: Why do you boast in the valleys? Flowing [is] your valley, the daughter the faithless, the [one] trusting in her treasures: Who will come against me?
pieces: Why do you boast of your valleys, \q your valley so rich, \q you faithless daughter? \q You trust in your treasures \q and say, "Who would come against me?"

L.4: Why do you boast of the valleys, \q your valley flowing, \q faithless daughter, \q who trusts in her treasures: \q "Who will come against me?"

R.4: Why do you brag about your valleys, \q your rich, fertile valleys, \q you unfaithful daughter? \q You trust in your wealth \q and say, "Who would dare to attack me?"

decisions.choice: your valley flowing: the valley rich and fruitful
alternatives: your valley is flowing away (its strength drains away)
your valley flows with blood
decisions.reason: The word means "flowing" and is used of a land flowing with milk and honey (Exodus 3:8). Here it most likely stands for the rich farmland of Ammon's valleys that the people were proud of. It could also mean that the valley's strength is draining away, or, as a warning, that it will run with the blood of the slain. The line is short and hard.

decisions.choice: faithless daughter: Ammon, personified as a daughter who has turned away
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Israel in 31:22, and the root runs through 3:14, 22 ("faithless children"). Here Ammon is a daughter who has gone her own way and trusts in her riches instead of God.

decisions.choice: "Who will come against me?": the proud boast of Ammon, quoted
decisions.reason: The last words are Ammon's own, a question that expects the answer "no one" (compare 21:13). Verse 5 answers it: God himself will bring terror on her.

decisions.choice: "Who will come against me?" set as quoted speech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no word for "saying"; the change of speaker is shown by the quotation marks, and Balanced and Readable add "and say".

records.source: הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא עָלַ֜יִךְ פַּ֗חַד נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת מִכָּל־סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] bringing on you terror, declares [the] Lord GOD of hosts, from all around you; and you will be driven out, each before him, and [there is] none gathering the fugitive.
pieces: I am about to bring terror on you from all who surround you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You will be driven away, each of you running headlong, \q and no one will gather those who flee.

L.5: Look, I am bringing terror upon you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts, from all who are around you; \q and you will be driven out, each one straight ahead, \q and no one will gather the fugitives.

R.5: I am going to bring terror on you from all the peoples around you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q You will all be chased away, each running for your life, \q and no one will bring the scattered people back together.

decisions.choice: each before him: each running straight ahead, without looking back
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of soldiers charging straight ahead (Joshua 6:5). Here it is panic: each person runs headlong for himself.

decisions.choice: no one gathering the fugitives: the scattered will not be brought back together
decisions.reason: A defeated people might regroup around a leader who rallied the survivors. Ammon will have none. This answers Ammon's boast in verse 4.

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD of hosts / of Armies
decisions.reason: As in the Isaiah and Jeremiah tables: the Lord with the divine name, "of hosts" at Literal and "of Armies" at Balanced and Readable.

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־שְׁב֥וּת בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And after so I will turn the turning of [the] sons of Ammon, declares the LORD.
pieces: Yet afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: But after this I will restore the fortunes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: But later I will make things good again for the Ammonites, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: turn Ammon's ruin into well-being
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used for Israel and Judah in 30:3 (see the note there): a complete reversal of ruin. Jeremiah gives the same promise to Egypt (46:26), Moab (48:47) and Elam (49:39). The God who judges the nations will also restore them.

decisions.choice: the verse is part of the Hebrew text
alternatives: leave the verse out, with the Greek
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah does not have this verse, just as it lacks the promise to Moab in 48:47 (stated from general knowledge). See the note at 1:1 on the shorter Greek form of the book. This translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again for (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for this phrase wherever it returns in Jeremiah, as at 30:3.

records.source: לֶאֱד֗וֹם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַאֵ֥ין ע֛וֹד חָכְמָ֖ה בְּתֵימָ֑ן אָבְדָ֤ה עֵצָה֙ מִבָּנִ֔ים נִסְרְחָ֖ה חָכְמָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Concerning Edom. Thus says the LORD of hosts: [Is there] no more wisdom in Teman? Has perished counsel from [the] discerning? Has gone bad their wisdom?
pieces: Concerning Edom. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Is there no wisdom left in Teman? \q Have the wise run out of counsel? \q Has their wisdom turned sour?

L.7: Concerning Edom. Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Is there no more wisdom in Teman? \q Has counsel perished from the discerning? \q Has their wisdom gone bad?

R.7: About Edom. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q Are there no wise people left in Teman? \q Can the clever no longer give good advice? \q Has all their wisdom rotted away?

decisions.choice: Edom and Teman: the people descended from Esau, and one of their chief regions
decisions.reason: Edom lay south and east of the Dead Sea. Its people came from Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 36:1, 8), and Teman was named for Esau's grandson (Genesis 36:11). Teman was known for its wise men: Job's friend Eliphaz came from there (Job 2:11). The oracle on Edom runs from verse 7 to verse 22.

decisions.choice: the oracle on Edom shares much with Obadiah
decisions.reason: Much of verses 7-22 is close to the book of Obadiah, which is also about Edom: verses 9-10 match Obadiah 5-6, and verses 14-16 match Obadiah 1-4. Obadiah 8 also speaks of God destroying the wise men of Edom. Obadiah is not yet translated here; when it is, the two passages should be compared word by word.

decisions.choice: has their wisdom gone bad: has it spoiled, become useless
alternatives: has their wisdom spread itself out (and been lost)
has their wisdom been let loose (gone)
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It is used of something left over or hanging loose (Exodus 26:12), and in later Hebrew of food that spoils and smells. The sense is that the famous wisdom of Edom is gone or no longer of use.

decisions.choice: Have the wise run out of counsel?
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "has counsel perished from the discerning" into a natural English question with the same sense.

records.heading: Edom

records.source: נֻ֤סוּ הָפְנוּ֙ הֶעְמִ֣יקוּ לָשֶׁ֔בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֖י דְּדָ֑ן כִּ֣י אֵ֥יד עֵשָׂ֛ו הֵבֵ֥אתִי עָלָ֖יו עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיו׃
records.gloss: Flee, turn back, go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan; for [the] disaster of Esau I will bring on him, [the] time I punish him.
pieces: Run! Turn and flee! Hide deep in the ground, \q you who live in Dedan! \q For I am bringing disaster on Esau, the time when I punish him.

L.8: Flee, turn back, go down deep to dwell, \q inhabitants of Dedan! \q For I will bring the disaster of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him.

R.8: Run away! Turn back! Hide deep down out of sight, \q you people of Dedan! \q I am going to bring disaster on Esau's people, Edom. It is time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to punish them.

decisions.choice: Dedan: an Arabian trading people to the southeast of Edom
decisions.reason: Dedan was a center of the caravan trade in northwest Arabia (25:23; Isaiah 21:13; Ezekiel 25:13; 27:20). Its people are warned to keep away from Edom, or to get their caravans out of it, when judgment falls.

decisions.choice: go deep to dwell: hide in deep places, in caves or remote country
alternatives: settle far off
decisions.reason: The command is "make deep to dwell": go down into hiding places in the rocks, or go far into the desert, out of the way of the coming invader. The same words return in verse 30.

decisions.choice: Esau: Edom, the people descended from Esau
decisions.reason: Edom is called by the name of its ancestor Esau (Genesis 25:30; 36:1), as Israel is called Jacob. The verb "punish" is "visit": God comes to deal with Edom's wrongs.

decisions.choice: Esau's people, Edom
decisions.reason: Readable says that Esau stands for the nation Edom (m3), and uses "them" for the people.

records.source: אִם־בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ לֹ֥א יַשְׁאִ֖רוּ עֽוֹלֵל֑וֹת אִם־גַּנָּבִ֥ים בַּלַּ֖יְלָה הִשְׁחִ֥יתוּ דַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves in the night, they would destroy their sufficiency.
pieces: If grape pickers came to you, \q would they not leave a few grapes behind? \q If thieves came at night, they would ruin only as much as they wanted.

L.9: If grape gatherers came to you, \q would they not leave gleanings? \q If thieves [came] by night, they would destroy only what was enough for them.

R.9: When people pick grapes, \q they leave a few grapes behind. \q When thieves come at night, they take only what they want.

decisions.choice: the grape gatherers and the thieves: words shared with Obadiah 5
decisions.reason: Obadiah 5 has the same two pictures, in the other order (thieves first, then grape gatherers), and both there are questions. See the note at verse 7.

decisions.choice: gleanings: the few grapes left on the vine after the harvest
decisions.reason: The law told harvesters to leave what they missed for the poor (Leviticus 19:10; Deuteronomy 24:21). Even a full harvest or a burglary leaves something behind; verse 10 says that Edom will be left nothing.

decisions.choice: would they not leave ... they would destroy only what was enough for them: questions and statements that expect agreement
alternatives: read both halves as statements: grape gatherers leave no gleanings, thieves destroy all they can
decisions.reason: The first half is a question expecting "yes, they would leave some". The second half has no question word; its last word means "their sufficiency", what they need or want, so even thieves stop somewhere. Either way the point is the contrast with verse 10.

decisions.choice: [only] what was enough for them / only as much as they wanted
decisions.reason: The word "only" draws out the sense of "their sufficiency"; Literal brackets "came", which the second clause leaves out.

decisions.choice: When people pick grapes, they leave a few grapes behind
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it expects, to keep the sentence simple.

records.source: כִּֽי־אֲנִ֞י חָשַׂ֣פְתִּי אֶת־עֵשָׂ֗ו גִּלֵּ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־מִסְתָּרָ֔יו וְנֶחְבָּ֖ה לֹ֣א יוּכָ֑ל שֻׁדַּ֥ד זַרְע֛וֹ וְאֶחָ֥יו וּשְׁכֵנָ֖יו וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: For I, I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hidden places, and to hide he will not be able; destroyed [is] his seed and his brothers and his neighbors, and he [is] no more.
pieces: But I have stripped Esau bare; I have laid open his hiding places, \q and he cannot conceal himself. \q His children, his relatives and his neighbors are destroyed, and he is gone.

L.10: But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, \q and he will not be able to hide. \q His offspring is destroyed, and his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.

R.10: But I will strip Edom bare. I will uncover all the places where its people hide, \q so they cannot hide anymore. \q Their children, relatives and neighbors will be destroyed, and Edom will be gone.

decisions.choice: stripped bare, his hiding places uncovered: words close to Obadiah 6
decisions.reason: Obadiah 6 says, "How Esau has been searched out, his hidden treasures sought!" Here the hidden places may be the treasures, or the hiding places in the rocks where the people take refuge (verse 16). See the note at verse 7.

decisions.choice: I have stripped ... is destroyed: the completed form for what God will surely do
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for a completed action, but they describe the judgment still to come, as in verses 13-17. Speaking of it as done shows that it is certain.

decisions.choice: his brothers and his neighbors: Edom's kin and the peoples allied with it
decisions.reason: "Brothers" are kinsmen, the clans related to Edom; "neighbors" are the peoples around it, such as Dedan (verse 8). With the "seed", the children, the whole people perishes.

decisions.choice: I will strip ... will be destroyed
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verbs in the future, since they describe judgment to come (m2), and says "Edom" for Esau (verse 8).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers", since the word means kin in general, not only men. Literal keeps "brothers".

records.source: עָזְבָ֥ה יְתֹמֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֣י אֲחַיֶּ֑ה וְאַלְמְנֹתֶ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י תִּבְטָֽחוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Leave your fatherless; I will keep [them] alive; and your widows on me let them trust.
pieces: Leave your orphans behind; I will keep them alive. \q Let your widows trust in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.11: Leave your fatherless; I will keep [them] alive; \q and let your widows trust in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.11: Leave your children who have no father with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will keep them alive. \q Your widows can trust in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: God himself promises to care for Edom's orphans and widows
alternatives: a grim word: no men will be left to care for them, so only God remains
decisions.reason: The speaker is God ("I will keep them alive"). Even in judgment on Edom, he will care for those who have no protector, as he is "father of the fatherless and defender of widows" (Psalm 68:6; Deuteronomy 10:18). The words also show how complete the judgment is: the men are gone, and the orphans and widows are left.

decisions.choice: children who have no father ... with me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "fatherless" means and makes plain that they are left in God's care.

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִ֠נֵּה אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֨ין מִשְׁפָּטָ֜ם לִשְׁתּ֤וֹת הַכּוֹס֙ שָׁת֣וֹ יִשְׁתּ֔וּ וְאַתָּ֣ה ה֔וּא נָקֹ֖ה תִּנָּקֶ֑ה לֹ֣א תִנָּקֶ֔ה כִּ֥י שָׁתֹ֖ה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: For thus says the LORD: Look, [those] who not [was] their judgment to drink the cup, surely they will drink; and you, [are] you he [who] surely will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for surely you will drink.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, \q do you really think you will go unpunished? \q You will not go unpunished; \q you must drink it.

L.12: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, those whose sentence was not to drink the cup will surely drink [it]; \q and you, are you the one who will indeed go unpunished? \q You will not go unpunished, \q but you will surely drink [it].

R.12: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Even people who did not deserve to drink from the cup of punishment must drink it. \q So do you think you will escape punishment? \q You will not escape! \q You must drink it.

decisions.choice: the cup: the cup of God's wrath that the nations must drink
decisions.reason: In 25:15-29 Jeremiah is told to make the nations drink the cup of the wine of God's wrath, and Edom is on the list (25:21). The words here repeat 25:28-29: "you must drink", and "will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished".

decisions.choice: those whose sentence was not to drink the cup: people who did not deserve this judgment
alternatives: those who were not used to drinking the cup
decisions.reason: "Their judgment" is the sentence passed on them. If even those who had not earned the cup must drink it, Edom, which has earned it, cannot escape. The text does not say who these others are; the argument is from the lesser to the greater, as in 25:29, where judgment begins with the city that bears God's name.

decisions.choice: surely ... indeed ... surely: the repeated verb for emphasis
decisions.reason: Three times a verb is doubled with its own infinitive, a Hebrew way of stressing certainty: they will surely drink; will you indeed go free; you will surely drink.

decisions.choice: go unpunished, as 25:29
decisions.reason: The wording of the question and answer follows 25:29 at each level, since the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: the cup of punishment
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־לְשַׁמָּ֧ה לְחֶרְפָּ֛ה לְחֹ֥רֶב וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה בָצְרָ֑ה וְכָל־עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: For by myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that a horror, a reproach, a waste and a curse will become Bozrah; and all its cities will become ruins of perpetuity.
pieces: For I swear by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q that Bozrah will become a horror, a disgrace, a wasteland and a curse, \q and all its towns will be ruins forever.

L.13: For by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} I have sworn, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q that Bozrah will become a horror, a reproach, a waste and a curse; \q and all its cities will become ruins forever.

R.13: I swear by {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q that the city of Bozrah will become a horror, a disgrace, an empty waste and a curse. \q All the towns around it will lie in ruins forever.

decisions.choice: by myself I have sworn: God's most solemn oath
decisions.reason: There is no one greater for God to swear by, so he swears by himself (Genesis 22:16; Isaiah 45:23; Jeremiah 22:5). The oath makes the judgment certain.

decisions.choice: Bozrah: the chief city of Edom
decisions.reason: Bozrah was a fortress city in the north of Edom, home of one of its early kings (Genesis 36:33). It stands for the whole nation, as in Isaiah 34:6; 63:1; Amos 1:12.

decisions.choice: a horror, a reproach, a waste and a curse: Bozrah will be an object of shock and scorn, and a name used in cursing
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses lists like this for Judah (24:9; 42:18; 44:12) and for the nations (25:9, 18). A "curse" here is a name people use when they call down evil on someone: "may you become like Bozrah".

decisions.choice: horror ... curse, as the Jeremiah list wording
decisions.reason: "Horror" and "curse" are kept at every level, as the terms list asks; "reproach" is "disgrace" at Balanced and Readable, as in 42:18 and 44:12.

records.source: שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וְצִ֖יר בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שָׁל֑וּחַ הִֽתְקַבְּצוּ֙ וּבֹ֣אוּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְק֖וּמוּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: A report I have heard from the LORD, and an envoy among the nations [has been] sent: Gather together and come against her, and rise up for battle!
pieces: I have heard news from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q a messenger has been sent among the nations: \q "Gather together and attack her! \q Rise up for battle!"

L.14: I have heard a report from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and an envoy has been sent among the nations: \q "Gather together and come against her, \q and rise up for battle!"

R.14: I have heard a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q A messenger has been sent to the nations to say, \q "Join together and attack Edom! \q Get ready for battle!"

decisions.choice: words shared with Obadiah 1
decisions.reason: Obadiah 1 opens with almost the same lines: "We have heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Rise up, and let us rise against her for battle." Here the prophet says "I have heard", and the call to the nations is "gather together and come". Verses 14-16 as a whole match Obadiah 1-4. See the note at verse 7.

decisions.choice: I have heard: the prophet speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker is Jeremiah, who has received the news from God, as in 4:19-21; God speaks again in verse 15.

decisions.choice: an envoy: a messenger sent to summon the nations to war against Edom
decisions.reason: The word means an official messenger (Isaiah 18:2; Proverbs 25:13). His message is a call to arms; "her" is Edom, spoken of as a woman, like Bozrah.

decisions.choice: Edom
decisions.reason: Readable names the one attacked instead of "her" (m3).

records.source: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֖וּי בָּאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: For look, small I have made you among the nations, despised among humankind.
pieces: For see, I will make you small among the nations, \q despised by all people.

L.15: For look, I have made you small among the nations, \q despised among humankind.

R.15: I will make you weak and unimportant among the nations. \q Everyone will look down on you.

decisions.choice: small among the nations, despised: as Obadiah 2
decisions.reason: Obadiah 2 has the same words. Edom, proud of its high places (verse 16), will be made small and despised.

decisions.choice: I have made you small: the completed form for what God will surely do
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the completed form speaks of the coming judgment as already done.

decisions.choice: I will make
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the verb in the future, since the judgment is still to come (m2). Literal keeps "I have made".

records.source: תִּֽפְלַצְתְּךָ֞ הִשִּׁ֤יא אֹתָךְ֙ זְד֣וֹן לִבֶּ֔ךָ שֹֽׁכְנִי֙ בְּחַגְוֵ֣י הַסֶּ֔לַע תֹּפְשִׂ֖י מְר֣וֹם גִּבְעָ֑ה כִּֽי־תַגְבִּ֤יהַ כַּנֶּ֨שֶׁר֙ קִנֶּ֔ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אֽוֹרִידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Your terror has deceived you, [the] presumption of your heart, [you] dwelling in [the] clefts of the rock, holding [the] height of [the] hill; though you make high like the eagle your nest, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
pieces: The terror you strike into others and the pride of your heart have deceived you, \q you who live in the clefts of the rock, \q who hold the heights of the hill. \q Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, \q I will bring you down from there, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: The terror you cause has deceived you, the arrogance of your heart, \q you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, \q who hold the height of the hill. \q Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, \q from there I will bring you down, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: You think everyone is afraid of you, and your pride has fooled you. \q You live in hiding places in the rocky cliffs. \q You hold the tops of the hills. \q But even if you build your home as high as an eagle's nest, \q I will bring you down from there, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your terror: the fear you strike into others
alternatives: your horrible idol (the object of horror you worship)
the horror that will come on you
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It comes from a root meaning "shudder". It most likely means the dread Edom inspired in its neighbors, which made it feel safe. A related word means a hideous idol in 1 Kings 15:13, so some read "your idol has deceived you".

decisions.choice: the rock: Edom's rocky heights
alternatives: Sela, the name of a fortress city of Edom
decisions.reason: The word sela means a crag or cliff, and Edom's people lived in strongholds high in the rocky mountains. Sela was also the name of an Edomite fortress captured by Amaziah king of Judah (2 Kings 14:7), so the word may also hint at that city. The same words are in Obadiah 3.

decisions.choice: the clefts of the rock, the eagle's nest, "from there I will bring you down": as Obadiah 3-4
decisions.reason: Obadiah 3-4 has the same picture of Edom living in the clefts of the rock, building its nest high, and being brought down. Obadiah adds "though you set your nest among the stars"; Jeremiah adds the line about the height of the hill and the word "your terror". See the note at verse 7.

decisions.choice: You think everyone is afraid of you, and your pride has fooled you
decisions.reason: Readable makes the two subjects of "deceived" into two short clauses and explains "your terror" (m1).

decisions.choice: your home
decisions.reason: Readable says what the nest stands for: the people's high home in the mountains.

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֥ה אֱד֖וֹם לְשַׁמָּ֑ה כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכּוֹתֶֽהָ׃
records.gloss: And Edom will become a horror; everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss over all its blows.
pieces: Edom will become a horror; \q everyone who passes by \q will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all its wounds.

L.17: And Edom will become a horror; \q everyone who passes by it \q will be appalled and will hiss over all its blows.

R.17: Edom will become a horror. \q Everyone who passes by will be shocked. \q They will make fun of it because of all the disasters that have struck it.

decisions.choice: appalled and hiss: the same words as 19:8
decisions.reason: The line is used of Jerusalem in 19:8 and of Babylon in 50:13. Hissing or whistling was a gesture of scorn and shock at a ruin (18:16; 1 Kings 9:8).

decisions.choice: its blows: the wounds and disasters that have struck it
decisions.reason: The word means blows or wounds; here the strokes of judgment that have left Edom in ruins.

decisions.choice: hiss / hiss in scorn / make fun of
decisions.reason: The wording follows 19:8 at each level.

records.source: כְּֽמַהְפֵּכַ֞ת סְדֹ֧ם וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וּשְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: As [the] overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbors, says the LORD, will not dwell there anyone, and will not sojourn in it a son of man.
pieces: As when Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them were overthrown, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there; \q no human being will settle in it.

L.18: As at the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there, \q and no {{gender:human being|son of man}} will sojourn in it.

R.18: Edom will be destroyed like Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q No one will live there. \q No one will even stay there for a while.

decisions.choice: the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah: the classic picture of a land destroyed for ever
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:24-29 tells how the cities of the plain were overturned. Deuteronomy 29:22, Isaiah 13:19 and Amos 4:11 use the same picture. This sentence returns almost word for word in 50:40, of Babylon, and its second half in 49:33, of Hazor.

decisions.choice: live ... sojourn: no one will settle there, not even for a short stay
decisions.reason: The second verb means to live somewhere as a newcomer or for a time. Edom will not even have passing visitors who stay.

decisions.choice: human being / son of man
decisions.reason: "Son of man" is a Hebrew way of saying a human being; the gender setting gives the traditional form at Literal. Readable says "no one".

records.source: הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־אַרְגִּ֤יעָה אֲרִיצֶ֨נּוּ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֨וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יֹעִידֶ֔נִּי וּמִי־זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: Look, like a lion he goes up from [the] thicket of the Jordan to [the] pasture of [the] ever-flowing; for in a moment I will make him run from it, and whoever [is] chosen over it I will appoint; for who [is] like me, and who will summon me, and who [is] this shepherd who will stand before me?
pieces: Look, an enemy will come up like a lion from the thick brush along the Jordan \q against the pastures that never run dry. \q In an instant I will chase Edom from its land, \q and I will set over it the one I choose. \q For who is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Who can call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to account? \q What shepherd can stand against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

L.19: Look, like a lion he comes up from the thicket of the Jordan \q to the ever-flowing pasture; \q for in an instant I will make him run from it, \q and whoever is chosen I will appoint over it. \q For who is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and who will summon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q And who is this shepherd who can stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

R.19: An enemy will come like a lion out of the thick bushes along the Jordan River \q to attack sheep in their green fields. \q In a moment I will chase the people of Edom out of their land. \q Then I will put the one I choose in charge of it. \q No one is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one can challenge {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q No ruler can stand up against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: like a lion from the thicket of the Jordan: the enemy attacks like a lion from its lair
decisions.reason: The thick growth along the Jordan was home to lions (12:5; Zechariah 11:3), and Jeremiah pictures the invader as a lion before (4:7). Verses 19-21 return almost word for word in 50:44-46, there of Babylon.

decisions.choice: he comes up ... I will make him run from it: the enemy attacks, and God drives Edom out of its land
alternatives: I will make them (the flock) run from it
I will make him (the lion) run from it
decisions.reason: The subject of "comes up" is not named; it is the invader of verses 14 and 22. The "him" whom God makes run is most likely Edom, the flock in the pasture, chased from its land. The words are short and could also mean that God makes the lion run off its prey.

decisions.choice: who will summon me? what shepherd can stand before me?: no one can challenge God
decisions.reason: To "summon" is to call someone to court to answer a charge. A shepherd is a ruler, as in 25:34-36. No people or king can bring God to trial or stand against him.

decisions.choice: whoever is chosen I will appoint over it: God will set over Edom the one he chooses
alternatives: I will appoint over it my chosen one
decisions.reason: God decides who will rule the land after Edom is driven out.

decisions.choice: an enemy ... Edom
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one who comes up and the one chased out (m2), so that the lion is not read as God.

decisions.choice: No one is like me ... No ruler can stand up against me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply, and says "ruler" for "shepherd" (m3).

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־אֱד֔וֹם וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵימָ֑ן אִם־לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נְוֵהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore hear [the] plan of the LORD that he has planned against Edom, and his purposes that he has purposed against [the] inhabitants of Teman: surely they will drag them, [the] little ones of the flock; surely he will make desolate over them their pasture.
pieces: So hear the plan {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made against Edom, \q the purposes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has formed \q against the people of Teman: \q even the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make their pasture a desolate place because of them.

L.20: Therefore hear the plan of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned against Edom, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purposes \q that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: \q surely they will drag them away, the little ones of the flock; \q surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make their pasture desolate because of them.

R.20: So listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has planned against Edom, \q what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided to do \q to the people of Teman. \q Even the youngest lambs of the flock will be dragged away. \q He will turn their fields into an empty waste.

decisions.choice: surely ... surely: an oath form, "if not"
decisions.reason: The words are literally "if not", the beginning of an oath whose end is left unsaid ("may it happen to me if they do not ..."). It means "they surely will".

decisions.choice: they will drag them away, the little ones of the flock: even the weakest of Edom's people will be carried off
alternatives: the smallest of the flock (the weakest enemies) will drag them away
decisions.reason: "The little ones of the flock" most likely names those dragged off: Edom is the flock, and even its lambs will be taken. The words could also be the subject, meaning that the weakest of the invaders will drag Edom away. The same words are in 50:45.

decisions.choice: he will make their pasture desolate because of them: Edom's land will be laid waste
alternatives: their pasture will be appalled at them
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for being appalled in verse 17; with a land as its object it means to make it a desolate waste. The pasture is the land where the flock lived.

decisions.choice: will be dragged away
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive, since the ones who drag are not named (m2).

records.source: מִקּ֣וֹל נִפְלָ֔ם רָעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ צְעָקָ֕ה בְּיַם־ס֖וּף נִשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: From [the] sound of their fall trembles the earth; a cry, at [the] Sea of Reeds is heard its sound.
pieces: At the sound of their fall \q the earth shakes; \q their cry is heard as far as the Red Sea.

L.21: At the sound of their fall \q the earth quakes; \q a cry! Its sound is heard at the Sea of Reeds.

R.21: When Edom falls, \q the noise will make the earth shake. \q People will hear the screaming as far away as the Red Sea.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the Red Sea, here its Gulf of Aqaba south of Edom
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "Sea of Reeds". It is the sea Israel crossed (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), and it also names the Gulf of Aqaba, the arm of the Red Sea at the southern end of Edom's land (1 Kings 9:26). The cry of Edom's fall carries to the far edge of its land.

decisions.choice: a cry, its sound is heard: the sound of Edom's cry
decisions.reason: The line is abrupt: "a cry" stands alone, then "its sound" is heard. The sound is the outcry of the falling nation. The same verse returns in 50:46, there of Babylon.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Exodus, Literal keeps "Sea of Reeds" and Balanced and Readable give the familiar name.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה כַנֶּ֨שֶׁר֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה וְיִדְאֶ֔ה וְיִפְרֹ֥שׂ כְּנָפָ֖יו עַל־בָּצְרָ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י אֱדוֹם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Look, like the eagle he will go up and swoop and spread his wings over Bozrah; and will be [the] heart of [the] warriors of Edom in that day like [the] heart of a woman in labor.
pieces: Look! Like an eagle he rises and swoops down \q and spreads his wings over Bozrah. \q On that day the warriors of Edom will have hearts \q like the heart of a woman in labor.

L.22: Look, like an eagle he will mount up and swoop down, \q and spread his wings over Bozrah; \q and the heart of the warriors of Edom on that day will be \q like the heart of a woman in labor.

R.22: Look! The enemy will fly up and swoop down like an eagle \q and spread his wings over Bozrah. \q On that day the soldiers of Edom will be terrified, \q like a woman giving birth.

decisions.choice: the eagle over Bozrah and the woman in labor: the same words as 48:40-41, of Moab
decisions.reason: The oracle on Moab uses this verse of Moab's towns (48:40-41). Here the eagle spreads its wings over Bozrah, Edom's chief city (verse 13). The Hebrew of the two verses is almost the same.

decisions.choice: the eagle: a great bird of prey, the eagle or the vulture
alternatives: vulture
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers the large birds of prey, both eagles and vultures (Micah 1:16). It pictures the invader, swift and sudden (4:13; Deuteronomy 28:49). The same bird stands for Edom's pride in verse 16; now it is the enemy.

decisions.choice: the heart of a woman in labor: helpless terror
decisions.reason: Jeremiah often compares the panic of the defeated to a woman's pain in childbirth (4:31; 6:24; 22:23; 30:6). The "heart" is courage: the warriors lose it entirely.

decisions.choice: the wording of 48:40-41; the enemy (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the wording of 48:40-41, where the Hebrew is the same, adding only "mount up" or "rises" for the verb this verse adds, and Bozrah and Edom for Moab. As in 48:40, Readable names the one who comes like an eagle, the invader; Literal and Balanced keep "he".

records.source: לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק בּ֤וֹשָֽׁה חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד כִּי־שְׁמֻעָ֥ה רָעָ֛ה שָׁמְע֖וּ נָמֹ֑גוּ בַּיָּ֣ם דְּאָגָ֔ה הַשְׁקֵ֖ט לֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃
records.gloss: Concerning Damascus. Are put to shame Hamath and Arpad, for bad news they have heard; they melt; in the sea [there is] anxiety; to be quiet it is not able.
pieces: Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are dismayed, \q for they have heard bad news, and their courage melts. \q They are troubled like the sea, \q which cannot be still.

L.23: Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, \q for they have heard bad news; they melt away. \q There is anxiety in the sea; \q it cannot be quiet.

R.23: About Damascus. The people of Hamath and Arpad are ashamed and afraid. \q They have heard bad news, and they have lost all courage. \q They are as restless as the stormy sea, \q which can never be calm.

decisions.choice: Damascus, Hamath and Arpad: the chief cities of the Aramean kingdoms of Syria
decisions.reason: Damascus was the capital of Aram, Israel's neighbor to the northeast (Isaiah 7:8; 17:1). Hamath, on the Orontes, and Arpad, in the north, were Aramean cities named together in Isaiah 10:9; 36:19; 37:13. They hear of Damascus's fall and lose heart. The oracle on Damascus runs from verse 23 to verse 27.

decisions.choice: in the sea there is anxiety: the people are as restless as the sea
alternatives: like the sea (reading a Hebrew letter that looks similar)
there is anxiety by the sea (among people living on the coast)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "in the sea". Read as it stands, it pictures the troubled sea that cannot rest (Isaiah 57:20). Many read "like the sea", which differs by one similar letter in Hebrew and makes the comparison plain. Either way the people are as restless as the sea.

decisions.choice: they melt: their courage dissolves
decisions.reason: "Melting" is a common picture of losing heart in fear (Exodus 15:15; Joshua 2:9, 24).

decisions.choice: They are troubled like the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the comparison that the line means, with the sense set out in m2; Literal keeps "in the sea".

records.heading: Damascus, Kedar and Elam

records.source: רָפְתָ֥ה דַמֶּ֛שֶׂק הִפְנְתָ֥ה לָנ֖וּס וְרֶ֣טֶט׀הֶחֱזִ֑יקָה צָרָ֧ה וַחֲבָלִ֛ים אֲחָזַ֖תָּה כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: Has grown weak Damascus; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized [her]; distress and pangs have taken hold of her like [a woman] giving birth.
pieces: Damascus has lost her strength; she has turned to run, and panic has taken hold of her; \q distress and pain grip her like a woman in labor.

L.24: Damascus has grown weak; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized [her]; \q distress and pangs have taken hold of her, like [a woman] giving birth.

R.24: The people of Damascus have no strength left. They turn to run away in panic. \q They are in pain and agony like a woman giving birth.

decisions.choice: distress and pangs like a woman giving birth: helpless terror
decisions.reason: As in verse 22, the city's panic is pictured as a woman's pain in childbirth (6:24; 22:23). Damascus is spoken of as a woman.

decisions.choice: The people of Damascus
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of the people instead of the city as a woman.

records.source: אֵ֥יךְ לֹֽא־עֻזְּבָ֖ה עִ֣יר תְּהִלָּ֑ת קִרְיַ֖ת מְשׂוֹשִֽׂי׃
records.gloss: How not forsaken [is the] city of praise, [the] town of my joy!
pieces: Why has the city of renown not been abandoned, \q the town of my joy?

L.25: How is it not forsaken, the city of praise, \q the town of my joy?

R.25: Why did the people not leave that famous city, \q the town that made me so glad?

decisions.choice: How is it not forsaken: why was the famous city not left (so that its people escaped) before it fell
alternatives: How the city of praise is forsaken! (reading without "not")
How the city of praise is not spared!
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "not": "how is it not forsaken". The best sense is a question of grief: why did its people not abandon the city and flee while they could? Verse 26 follows with "therefore its young men will fall". The Latin Vulgate translates without "not" ("how they have forsaken the city of praise"), which gives a cry of lament over the abandoned city (stated from general knowledge). The traditional Hebrew text also differs between the letters and the reading tradition on the form of "praise", without change of sense.

decisions.choice: the town of my joy: the speaker is someone who loved Damascus
alternatives: the joy of the people of Damascus
the prophet's or God's words
decisions.reason: "My joy" may be the words of a citizen of Damascus mourning the city, or of the prophet taking up their lament. Some ancient translations lack "my".

decisions.choice: Why ... the city of renown / that famous city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "why" for the Hebrew "how" of a sorrowful question (m1), and "renown" or "famous" for "praise", a city that others praised.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה יִדַּ֨מּוּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Therefore will fall her young men in her squares, and all [the] men of war will be silenced in that day, declares the LORD of hosts.
pieces: So her young men will fall in her streets, \q and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.26: Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, \q and all the men of war will be silenced on that day, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.26: So the young men of Damascus will be killed in the streets. \q All its soldiers will die on that day, \q says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: young men falling in the squares, the soldiers silenced: a line repeated of Babylon in 50:30
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Babylon in 50:30. "Be silenced" means to be cut down in death (8:14; 25:37).

decisions.choice: her squares: the open places inside the city gates
decisions.reason: The squares were the broad open spaces where people met and traded. The fighting reaches the heart of the city.

records.source: וְהִצַּ֥תִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת בֶּן־הֲדָֽד׃ס
records.gloss: And I will kindle a fire on [the] wall of Damascus, and it will consume [the] strongholds of Ben-hadad.
pieces: I will set fire to the wall of Damascus, \q and it will burn up the fortresses of Ben-hadad.

L.27: And I will kindle a fire on the wall of Damascus, \q and it will consume the strongholds of Ben-hadad.

R.27: I will set the walls of Damascus on fire. \q The fire will burn down the strong palaces of King Ben-hadad.

decisions.choice: fire on the wall, consuming the strongholds of Ben-hadad: the words of Amos 1:4, 14
decisions.reason: Amos 1:4 says of Damascus, "I will send a fire on the house of Hazael, and it will consume the strongholds of Ben-hadad", and Amos 1:14 "I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah". Jeremiah takes up Amos's words against the same city. Amos is not yet translated here; when it is, the two lines should be compared.

decisions.choice: Ben-hadad: the name of several kings of Damascus
decisions.reason: Ben-hadad, "son of Hadad" (the storm god of Aram), was the name of kings of Damascus in the time of Asa, Ahab and Jehoash (1 Kings 15:18; 20:1; 2 Kings 13:24-25). Their strongholds are the fortified palaces of the royal city.

decisions.choice: King Ben-hadad
decisions.reason: Readable adds "King" so that the name is understood.

records.source: לְקֵדָ֣ר׀וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ אֶל־קֵדָ֔ר וְשָׁדְד֖וּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: Concerning Kedar and concerning [the] kingdoms of Hazor, which struck Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. Thus says the LORD: Arise, go up against Kedar, and devastate [the] sons of [the] east!
pieces: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon defeated. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Rise up, march against Kedar, \q and destroy the people of the east!

L.28: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon struck down. \q Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Arise, go up against Kedar, \q and devastate the {{gender:children|sons}} of the east!

R.28: About Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon attacked and defeated. \q This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Get up and attack Kedar! \q Destroy the desert tribes of the east!

decisions.choice: Kedar: Arab tribes of the desert east of Israel
decisions.reason: Kedar was descended from Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). Its people lived in tents with their flocks and camels in the Syrian and Arabian desert (2:10; Isaiah 21:16-17; 60:7; Psalm 120:5; Ezekiel 27:21). The oracle on Kedar and Hazor runs from verse 28 to verse 33. The heading is prose; the oracle that follows is poetry.

decisions.choice: the kingdoms of Hazor: settled groups of the Arabian desert, not the city of Hazor in Galilee
alternatives: the city of Hazor in northern Israel (Joshua 11:1)
decisions.reason: This Hazor is not the old Canaanite city in Galilee. The word is related to the word for unwalled villages, and Isaiah 42:11 speaks of "the villages that Kedar inhabits". Here it seems to name the small chiefdoms of village-dwelling Arabs, set beside Kedar's tent-dwelling tribes. Verses 30-33 speak of them as a people without walls.

decisions.choice: which Nebuchadrezzar struck down: Babylon's campaign against the Arab tribes
decisions.reason: Babylonian records tell of a campaign by Nebuchadrezzar against the Arabs of the desert in about 599 BC (stated from general knowledge). The heading names the attacker that verses 28-33 call to the attack. The Hebrew spells his name Nebuchadrezzar here, as often in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: the sons of the east: the peoples of the desert east of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase names the nomad peoples of the eastern desert (Judges 6:3; Job 1:3; Isaiah 11:14).

decisions.choice: the desert tribes of the east
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "sons of the east" were (m4).

records.source: אָהֳלֵיהֶ֤ם וְצֹאנָם֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ יְרִיעוֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְכָל־כְּלֵיהֶ֛ם וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם יִשְׂא֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְקָרְא֧וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם מָג֖וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: Their tents and their flock they will take; their curtains and all their goods and their camels they will carry off for themselves; and they will call to them: Terror [is] on every side!
pieces: Their tents and their flocks will be seized; \q their tent curtains, all their goods and their camels will be carried off. \q People will shout at them, "Terror on every side!"

L.29: Their tents and their flocks they will take; \q their curtains and all their goods and their camels they will carry off for themselves; \q and they will call out against them, "Terror on every side!"

R.29: Their enemies will take their tents and flocks. \q They will carry off their tent curtains, all their goods and their camels. \q They will shout at them, "Terror all around!"

decisions.choice: tents, curtains, camels: the whole wealth of a desert people
decisions.reason: The tent curtains were woven of black goat hair (Song of Songs 1:5, "the tents of Kedar"; Isaiah 54:2). With their flocks and camels, these were all that nomads owned.

decisions.choice: Terror on every side: Jeremiah's repeated cry
decisions.reason: The words are Jeremiah's own refrain (6:25; 20:3, 10; 46:5). Here the attackers shout it at the fleeing tribes.

decisions.choice: Terror on every side / Terror all around
decisions.reason: One wording at each level for the refrain, as in 6:25 and 20:10.

decisions.choice: will be seized / Their enemies will take
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they will take" without naming who; Balanced uses the passive and Readable names the enemies.

records.source: נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָשֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָעַ֨ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ עֵצָ֔ה וְחָשַׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַחֲשָׁבָֽה׃
records.gloss: Flee, wander far away, go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Hazor, declares the LORD; for has planned against you Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon a plan, and he has devised against you a purpose.
pieces: Run! Get far away! Hide deep in the ground, you who live in Hazor, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q For Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you; \q he has worked out a scheme against you.

L.30: Flee, wander far away, go down deep to dwell, inhabitants of Hazor, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you, \q and has devised a purpose against you.

R.30: Run away! Go far off! Hide deep down out of sight, you people of Hazor, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has made plans to attack you. \q He has decided what he will do to you.

decisions.choice: go deep to dwell: hide in deep places
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, said there to Dedan.

decisions.choice: a plan ... a purpose: the king's plan against them
decisions.reason: The words are the ones used for the LORD's plan against Edom in verse 20. Nebuchadrezzar's plan carries out what God has spoken (25:9).

decisions.choice: Hide deep in the ground / Hide deep down out of sight
decisions.reason: The same wording as verse 8.

records.source: ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ אֶל־גּ֥וֹי שְׁלֵ֛יו יוֹשֵׁ֥ב לָבֶ֖טַח נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־דְלָתַ֧יִם וְלֹֽא־בְרִ֛יחַ ל֖וֹ בָּדָ֥ד יִשְׁכֹּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Arise, go up against a nation at ease, dwelling in security, declares the LORD; not gates and not bar [are] to it; alone they dwell.
pieces: Rise up and attack a nation at ease, living without a care, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q a nation with no gates and no bars, whose people live by themselves.

L.31: Arise, go up against a nation at ease, that dwells in security, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q it has neither gates nor bar; they dwell alone.

R.31: Get up and attack a nation that feels safe and has no worries, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Its people have no city gates or bars to lock them. They live far away from everyone else.

decisions.choice: no gates or bars, living alone: unwalled camps far from other peoples
decisions.reason: Desert tribes and villages had no city walls, gates or bars to shut them (Ezekiel 38:11). They felt safe because they lived far from others, as Laish did before it was taken (Judges 18:7, 27).

decisions.choice: at ease, dwelling in security: carefree, expecting no attack
decisions.reason: The words describe a people who feel no danger. Their very ease makes them easy prey.

decisions.choice: city gates or bars to lock them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bars were for.

records.source: וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם לָבַ֗ז וַהֲמ֤וֹן מִקְנֵיהֶם֙ לְשָׁלָ֔ל וְזֵרִתִ֥ים לְכָל־ר֖וּחַ קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֑ה וּמִכָּל־עֲבָרָ֛יו אָבִ֥יא אֶת־אֵידָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will become their camels plunder, and [the] abundance of their livestock spoil; and I will scatter them to every wind, [those] clipped [at the] corner, and from all its sides I will bring their disaster, declares the LORD.
pieces: Their camels will become plunder and their great herds spoil; \q I will scatter to every wind those who clip the hair at their temples, \q and I will bring disaster on them from every side, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: And their camels will become plunder, and the abundance of their livestock spoil; \q and I will scatter to every wind those who are clipped [at the] corners, \q and from every side of it I will bring their disaster, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: Their camels and their great herds of cattle will be taken as plunder. \q I will scatter in every direction the desert tribes who cut their hair short at the sides. \q I will bring disaster on them from every side, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: clipped at the corners: tribes who cut the hair at the sides of the head
decisions.reason: The same people are described this way in 9:25 and 25:23. Some desert tribes trimmed the hair at the temples, a custom the law forbade Israel (Leviticus 19:27).

decisions.choice: scatter to every wind: drive them away in every direction
decisions.reason: The winds stand for the directions of the compass, as in verse 36.

decisions.choice: clipped at the corners, as 9:25 and 25:23
decisions.reason: The wording follows 9:25 and 25:23 at each level.

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And will become Hazor a haunt of jackals, a desolation until forever; will not dwell there anyone, and will not sojourn in it a son of man.
pieces: Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a wasteland forever. \q No one will live there; \q no human being will settle in it.

L.33: And Hazor will become a lair of jackals, a desolation forever; \q no one will live there, \q and no {{gender:human being|son of man}} will sojourn in it.

R.33: Hazor will become a ruin where only jackals live. It will be empty forever. \q No one will live there. \q No one will even stay there for a while.

decisions.choice: a haunt of jackals: the picture of a ruin left to wild animals
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses it of Judah's towns and Jerusalem (9:10; 10:22) and of Babylon (51:37). The second half of the verse repeats verse 18, said there of Edom (and in 50:40 of Babylon).

decisions.choice: lair / haunt of jackals, as 10:22
decisions.reason: The wording follows 10:22, and the last two lines follow verse 18.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־עֵילָ֑ם בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: That which came [as the] word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in [the] beginning of [the] reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
pieces: This message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet Jeremiah about Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:

L.34: That which came [as] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at [the] beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:

R.34: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the prophet Jeremiah about Elam. It came early in the time when Zedekiah was king of Judah:

decisions.choice: Elam: a kingdom far to the east, beyond Babylon
decisions.reason: Elam lay east of the Tigris, in what is now southwestern Iran, with its capital at Susa (Genesis 10:22; 14:1; Daniel 8:2). Its archers were known in Israel (Isaiah 22:6). It was among the nations to drink the cup in 25:25. The oracle on Elam runs from verse 34 to verse 39.

decisions.choice: at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah: about 597 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar made Zedekiah king after taking Jehoiachin to Babylon (2 Kings 24:17). The same date is given in 27:1 and 28:1. This heading is prose, unlike the poetry of the oracle.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew order and form of the heading
alternatives: the Greek order, with the oracle on Elam first and the date at its end
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation the oracle on Elam is the first of the oracles against the nations, placed right after 25:13, and its date ("at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah") stands at its end (stated from general knowledge). See the note at 1:1. This translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the heading wording as 14:1 (Literal) and 46:1 (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal follows 14:1, which has the same Hebrew form; Balanced and Readable follow 46:1 and 47:1, which use the book's word "message"; and "the beginning of the reign" follows 27:1 and 28:1.

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י שֹׁבֵ֖ר אֶת־קֶ֣שֶׁת עֵילָ֑ם רֵאשִׁ֖ית גְּבוּרָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Look, I [am] breaking [the] bow of Elam, [the] first of their might.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q I am going to break the bow of Elam, \q the mainstay of their strength.

L.35: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, \q the chief of their might.

R.35: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q I will break the bows of Elam's archers. \q They are the main strength of Elam's army.

decisions.choice: the bow of Elam: Elam's famous archers
decisions.reason: Elam's soldiers were known as bowmen (Isaiah 22:6). To break the bow is to destroy a nation's power to fight (Hosea 1:5; Psalm 46:10).

decisions.choice: the first of their might: the chief part, the mainstay of their strength
alternatives: the first fruits of their strength
decisions.reason: "First" means the best or chief part. The bow was the heart of Elam's strength.

decisions.choice: Elam's archers ... Elam's army
decisions.reason: Readable says that the bow stands for the archers and the army (m1).

records.source: וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י אֶל־עֵילָ֜ם אַרְבַּ֣ע רוּח֗וֹת מֵֽאַרְבַּע֙ קְצ֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְזֵ֣רִתִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל הָרֻח֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה הַגּ֔וֹי אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא שָׁ֖ם נִדְּחֵ֥י עֵילָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will bring against Elam four winds from [the] four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds; and there will not be the nation where will not come there [the] outcasts of Elam.
pieces: I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four ends of the heavens, \q and I will scatter its people \q to all these winds. \q There will not be a nation \q that Elam's exiles do not reach.

L.36: And I will bring upon Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, \q and I will scatter them \q to all these winds; \q and there will be no nation \q to which the outcasts of Elam will not come.

R.36: I will bring winds against Elam from every direction. \q I will scatter its people everywhere. \q Its exiles will be found in every nation on earth.

decisions.choice: four winds from the four ends of the heavens: from every direction
decisions.reason: The four winds are the four points of the compass (Ezekiel 37:9; Daniel 7:2; Zechariah 2:10). Judgment comes on Elam from every side, and its people are scattered in every direction.

decisions.choice: the outcasts of Elam
alternatives: the outcasts of long ago (the letters as written)
decisions.reason: The letters of the traditional text could be read as the word for "forever" or "long ago"; the reading tradition, followed here, has "Elam", which fits the verse.

decisions.choice: its people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are: the people of Elam.

decisions.choice: Its exiles will be found in every nation on earth
decisions.reason: Readable turns the double negative ("no nation where the exiles will not come") into a plain statement with the same meaning.

records.source: וְהַחְתַּתִּ֣י אֶת־עֵ֠ילָם לִפְנֵ֨י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֜ם וְלִפְנֵ֣י׀מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֧ם׀רָעָ֛ה אֶת־חֲר֥וֹן אַפִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will terrify Elam before their enemies and before [those] seeking their life, and I will bring on them disaster, [the] burning of my anger, declares the LORD; and I will send after them the sword until I have consumed them.
pieces: I will fill Elam with terror before their enemies, before those who want them dead. I will bring disaster on them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fierce anger, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will send the sword after them \q until I have finished them off.

L.37: And I will terrify Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life, and I will bring disaster upon them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burning anger, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q and I will send the sword after them \q until I have consumed them.

R.37: I will make the people of Elam terrified of their enemies, who want to kill them. In {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fierce anger I will bring disaster on them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will send war after them \q until I have wiped them out.

decisions.choice: I will terrify: I will shatter their courage
alternatives: I will shatter Elam (break it)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken or dismayed, and here to make Elam break down in fear before its enemies (1:17; Isaiah 30:31).

decisions.choice: disaster, my burning anger: the disaster is God's anger at work
decisions.reason: "My burning anger" stands beside "disaster" to say what the disaster is (25:37-38; 30:24).

decisions.choice: send the sword after them until I have consumed them: pursue them with war to the end
decisions.reason: The same words are said of Judah's exiles in 9:15. The sword follows them even after they flee.

decisions.choice: war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as in 25:29.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י כִסְאִ֖י בְּעֵילָ֑ם וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֛ם מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy from there king and princes, declares the LORD.
pieces: I will set up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne in Elam \q and destroy the king and officials there, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.38: And I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne in Elam, \q and I will destroy from there king and princes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.38: I will set up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne in Elam to judge it and rule over it. \q I will destroy its king and its leaders, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I will set my throne in Elam: God takes his seat as judge and ruler over Elam
decisions.reason: A conqueror set his throne in a captured land to pass sentence and rule it (1:15; 43:10). God himself does so in Elam: its own king and princes are removed, and he rules there.

decisions.choice: to judge it and rule over it
decisions.reason: Readable says what setting up a throne means (m1).

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: As in the Isaiah and Jeremiah tables for sar.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־שְׁב֥וּת עֵילָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be in [the] latter of the days [that] I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.
pieces: Yet in days to come I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.39: And it will be in the latter days [that] I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.39: But in the days to come I will make things good again for Elam, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: in the latter days: in the time to come
decisions.reason: The phrase looks to a time beyond the judgment (23:20; 30:24; 48:47). It does not name a date.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes of Elam
decisions.reason: As in verse 6 for Ammon, and 30:3 for Israel and Judah: God will turn Elam's ruin into well-being. The traditional text's letters and reading tradition differ slightly on the spelling of both words here, with no change of sense.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again for (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6 and 30:3.

decisions.choice: in days to come
decisions.reason: As in 30:24.
